nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group with subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that $A$ is abelian, $B$ is locally quaternion, and $G = AB$, that is, every element of $G$ is a product $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$. Then $G$ is soluble.
nodes.title: Products of abelian and locally quaternion groups are soluble

nodes.summary: The proposition that every group $G$ with subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that $A$ is abelian, $B$ is locally quaternion, and $G = AB$ (every element of $G$ is a product $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$) is soluble.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.95 (Sozutov)

nodes.summary: A subgroup $B$ of a group $G$ is locally quaternion if there is a strictly increasing sequence $C_0 < C_1 < C_2 < \cdots$ of subgroups of $G$, each isomorphic to a generalized quaternion group $Q_{2^{k+2}}$ of order $2^{k+2}$ for some $k \ge 1$, whose supremum (for a chain, the union) is $B$. In particular $B$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Locally quaternion subgroup
